MINOR: Delta only demonstrates `authorityReasonBounded` usage in tests; the metric emission path in `backlogAuthority` is not shown to route reasons through the allowlist, so AC-1's "only bounded reasons" is enforced by assertion rather than by a fail-closed sanitizer at emit time — confirm production emits a fixed fallback (e.g. `internal_error`) for unbounded reasons.

Bounded reason set now lives as a second definition in `edpsvc` while the reason codes originate in `edpdata`; without a single exported source of truth the producer/consumer lists can drift and silently drop a legitimately new reason at the gauge.
`authorityReasons` is a mutable package-level `var`; any future `init`/test mutation changes runtime label policy globally. Prefer an immutable `switch`/`map` returned by an unexported accessor.
NIT: Only a single-level `%w` wrap of `*pgconn.PgError{57014}` is added; a doubly wrapped chain or an `errors.As`-only wrapper is still untested, so the structured-timeout assumption remains partially proven.

The new emission-count guard asserts at least one reason line exists but not that the failure classified as the expected `internal_error`; asserting the exact reason would catch misclassification regressions that the allowlist check still passes.
Dropped/unbounded reasons (if sanitized) have no counter, so operators cannot see that a label was rewritten — a small observability gap for diagnosing new error classes.
SUMMARY: Delta is narrow and resolves the prior three findings as claimed: shared allowlist, non-vacuous emission assertion, and wrapped pgconn coverage.
Remaining risks are about enforcement placement (test-time allowlist vs emit-time sanitization) and duplicated reason definitions across `edpdata`/`edpsvc`, not correctness of the delta.
No blockers or majors introduced; approve with the allowlist-wiring and single-source-of-truth items tracked as follow-ups.
